To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the achievable information rates (in bits/sec/Hz) and optimum code rate (in bits/channel/use) in the individual transmission channels of a WDM system are strongly asymmetric about the central channel in the presence of third order fiber nonlinearities.

the achievable information rates and optimum code rates are significantly asymmetric about the central channel in both EDFA- and Raman-amplified optical communication systems due to the presence third order dispersion, and the forward error correction codes have to be optimized on a per channel, asymmetric basis to maximize the overall system throughput.

the third order dispersion can be effectively compensated with a single channel digital nonlinearity compensator and the performance of such compensator is found to be independent of the modulation order.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of ultra wideband optical fiber communication systems with a capacity exceeding 10 Tb/s, which is the first step to realize the 100 Tb/s optical fiber communication systems in future.
the development of novel optical fiber communication systems and components for ultra high speed transmission.
the investigation of the impact of fiber nonlinearities and high order dispersion in ultra wideband optical communication systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the information rates and code rate optimization in ultra-wideband optical fiber communication systems accounting for high order fiber dispersion are essential to maximize the throughput of the systems.
the third order dispersion is a significant impairment for ultra wideband optical communication systems.

the impact of third-order dispersion on optical communication systems can be mitigated with digital signal processing techniques, and the achievable information rate and optimum code rate can be maximized with the proposed asymmetrically optimized forward error correction schemes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, the third order fiber dispersion can be effectively mitigated using a digital nonlinearity compensator, but it can also be exploited to improve the performance of a digital communication system by optimizing the code rates asymmetrically, on per channel basis.
the third order dispersion has to be taken into account for the accurate estimation of the information rate in the ultra wideband optical fiber communication systems.

, in order to achieve the highest throughput in the ultra high speed optical communication systems, it is necessary to consider the impact of the third order fiber dispersion and to design the forward error correction codes asymmetrically.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the third order dispersion can significantly impact the performance of the digital nonlinearity compensators and the forward error correction codes, which has to be accounted for in ultra wideband optical fiber communication systems.
the third order dispersion can be used as a tool for optimizing the forward error correction codes in the optical communication system.
the AIRs in both EDFA (C band) and Raman amplified (C+L band) systems are significantly lower than those predicted by the standard nonlinear Shannon capacity.
